messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: how many times is reduce$post evaluated per key
parts:
I thought the answer was 1 and exactly one, in some cases it is true and in some cases, putting a print statement in post, I see the same key twice, which of course breaks my programs. Test case

A = "/tmp/A"
B = "/tmp/B"
rhwrite(lapply(1:4, function(i) list(from=i,to=i+1)), A, 1)
> do.call(rbind, rhread(A))
About to unserialize 0.07 kb, please wait

[1,] 1    2   
[2,] 2    3   
[3,] 3    4   
[4,] 4    5   
rhcp(A,B)
rhex(
  rhmr(ifolder= c(A,B), 
    ofolder = "/tmp/rhout", 
    inout = c('sequence','sequence'), 
    map = expression({lapply(seq_along(map.keys), 
                                          function(i) {rhcollect(map.keys[[i]], map.values[[i]]);
                                                          rhcollect(map.values[[i]], map.keys[[i]])})}), 
    reduce = expression(
       pre = {},
       reduce={rhcollect(reduce.key, paste(reduce.values, sep = ":", collapse = ":"))}, 
       post={print(reduce.key)})))

This is the output of the print statement in post, mixed with regular hadoop messages

11/04/01 23:03:05 INFO rhipe.RHMRHelper: Reduce:Started external program:/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so --slave --silent --vanilla --max-ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G

11/04/01 23:03:06 INFO mapred.TaskRunner: Task:attempt_local_0001_r_000000_0 is done. And is in the process of commiting

Three keys are present twice. If we examine the output, we have


> do.call(rbind, rhread("/tmp/rhout/"))
About to unserialize 0.14 kb, please wait
     [,1] [,2] 
[1,] 2    "1:1"
[2,] 3    "2:2"

As you see, there are multiple records with the same key, which is not the expected behaviour. What am I missing? Thanks


Antonio

parts:
Hmm. Try this modification to post, Hadoop might run a task twice ...
but only collect one.
I made this change to post, if the post is run twice for a given
reduce,key this counter will be greater than 1.

post={
rhcounter(reduce.key,reduce.key,1)
}

Saptarshi

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] how many times is reduce$post evaluated per key
parts:
Hello,

I'd say we've made much progress! Your postscripts have answered your questions.
RHIPE in some sense is subtly typed, that is keys are compared in
Hadoop based on
comparing the byte representation. So integers are numerics are
different

> rhsz(1)
[1] 08 02 12 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 f0 3f
> rhsz(1L)
[1] 08 04 1a 01 02

Now, RHIPE is not doing any casting behind the scenes. In the line

X <- rhwrite(lapply(1:4, function(i) list(from=i,to=i+1)), A, 1)

rhwrite will check if the list has a names attribute
- if yes, that becomes reduce.keys
- if not, as.character(1:length(list)) becomes the keys
and if each element of the list is is list(a,b) it leaves it untouched
and write thes elements (like what you'd get from rhread) and this is
the case for X.

Anyway, in X, X[[1]][[1]] is an integer and X[[1]][[2]] is a numeric.
The X[[1]][[1]] is the
map.key and X[[1]][[2]] is the map.value.


Hope it helps

Saptarshi

parts:
Now, RHIPE is not doing any casting behind the scenes. In the line

X <- rhwrite(lapply(1:4, function(i) list(from=i,to=i+1)), A, 1)

rhwrite will check if the list has a names attribute
- if yes, that becomes reduce.keys
- if not, as.character(1:length(list)) becomes the keys
and if each element of the list is is list(a,b) it leaves it untouched
and write thes elements (like what you'd get from rhread) and this is
the case for X.

What it's doing in my case is using the first element of the inner list (from) as key and the second (to) as value. The first element is an integer and the second is numeric. The names are discarded.  See commands below. Thanks


Antonio

> rhread(A)
